title: Qingniao: The Blue-Green Birds of the Queen Mother of the West
metaDescription: Qingniao are birds associated with Xiwangmu, the Queen Mother of the West. Early descriptions of attendants and later messenger imagery should be read in their own contexts.
description: Qingniao are birds associated with Xiwangmu, the Queen Mother of the West. Early descriptions of attendants and later messenger imagery should be read in their own contexts.
storyHooks: Three messengers carry the same invitation, but each receives a different reply. Which response reaches the host?

sections.origin: The Shanhaijing describes three qing birds bringing food to Xiwangmu. The Wikisource text moves this passage between the northern and western inner-seas sections through its editorial arrangement; its notes explain the placement.
sections.legend: Taiping Yulan, volume 927, preserves another account under its bird material: a qing bird appears before Emperor Wu, in a passage attributed to Han Wu Gushi. This is part of the literary association between the birds and the Queen Mother.
sections.variants: The word qing covers a range often translated as blue or green. Calling the birds blue-green avoids pretending that the text supplies a precise modern paint colour. Three attendants also should not automatically become one uniquely named individual.
sections.culture: For reading and drawing, distinguish role from appearance: carrying food, announcing a visitor, and delivering a message are related ideas, but each needs its own textual support.

sources.title: Shanhaijing — Hai Nei Bei Jing, editorial notes on the three birds

researchNote: Based on online Chinese transcriptions and their commentary. This is not a critical edition or a claim that every messenger bird is Qingniao.

questions.question: Is Qingniao one bird or three?
questions.answer: The Shanhaijing passage describes three birds serving Xiwangmu. Other literary uses need to be read separately.

questions.question: Are the birds blue or green?
questions.answer: Qing can cover both; blue-green is used here to preserve that uncertainty.
